gait_changed.instructions: Has this person's walking pattern changed meaningfully compared with their own baseline?

real_fall.instructions: Did the wearer most likely have a real fall (as opposed to a bump, a dropped band, or nothing)?

suggest.instructions: Which single product from the catalog is the most relevant suggestion to show the family?

criteria.night_lights: Motion-activated night lights for hallway and bathroom.
criteria.cane: A walking cane for daytime walking support.
criteria.pill_organiser: A weekly pill organiser with alarms.

wearer_ok.instructions: After the 'did you fall?' prompt, what should the system do? Words marked with a low confidence may have been misheard.

criteria.cancel: The wearer clearly said or tapped that they are fine. Cancel the alert.
criteria.ask_again: The answer is unclear, missing words, or low confidence. Ask again or wait for a tap.
criteria.escalate: The wearer asked for help or clearly said they are not fine. Alert the family.

wearer_ok_v2.instructions: After the 'did you fall?' prompt, what should the system do? Only the wearer's own voice, a tap on the band, or a tap in the app counts as an answer. Speech from another voice (TV, radio, visitor) is not an answer. Words with low confidence may have been misheard.

criteria.cancel: The wearer themself clearly said or tapped that they are fine. Cancel the alert.
criteria.ask_again: No clear answer from the wearer yet. Ask again on the band and the app, and keep the timer running.
criteria.escalate: The wearer asked for help, said they are not fine, or there are signs of distress such as groaning or no movement. Alert the family.

fall_happened.instructions: Considering the motion data and everything heard from any voice, did the wearer most likely really fall?

tell_family.instructions: What should the family be told? Another person's words can be evidence of what happened, but only the wearer's own voice or tap can say that she is fine.

criteria.nothing: No fall happened. Tell the family nothing.
criteria.inform: A fall happened but the wearer is being helped or says she is fine. Tell the family calmly, not as an emergency.
criteria.emergency: A fall happened and nobody is confirmed to be helping, or someone asked for urgent help. Alert the family now.

cases.name: stable, all normal
cases.input: 14 days. Step-time ratio 1.03 to 1.05 every day, same as the month before. Cadence 108 to 110. No night-time walks. All pill reminders confirmed with a tap. No free-fall events.

cases.name: daytime limp only
cases.input: 14 days. Step-time ratio rose from 1.04 to 1.32 and stayed there on 13 of 14 days. Cadence down from 108 to 90. All walking between 9 am and 6 pm. No night-time walks. All pills confirmed. No free-fall events.

cases.name: night wandering only
cases.input: 14 days. Step-time ratio steady at 1.04, cadence steady at 107. Five walks between 2 and 4 am in a dark hallway, two brief stumbles answered 'I am fine' within 5 seconds. All pills confirmed.

cases.name: missed pills only
cases.input: 14 days. Gait steady: step-time ratio 1.04, cadence 109. No night walks, no free-fall events. Evening pill reminder not confirmed on 9 of 14 days; morning pills confirmed every day.

cases.name: real fall
cases.input: Today 3:10 pm. Free-fall event of 0.4 s followed by a 6 g impact, then band orientation changed from upright to horizontal and stayed there. No movement for 4 minutes. No answer to the 'did you fall?' prompt. Gait this week steady: ratio 1.04, cadence 108.

cases.name: band dropped on table
cases.input: Today 9:02 am. Free-fall event of 0.2 s and a 3 g impact. Two seconds earlier the band was taken off (no motion consistent with wearing). Afterwards it lay perfectly still on a flat surface for 30 minutes, then was put back on and normal walking resumed. Gait steady: ratio 1.05.

cases.name: bumped the door
cases.input: Today 11:15 am. Single 2.5 g spike on the wrist while walking, no free-fall phase. Walking continued without pause at cadence 106. Tapped 'I am fine'. Gait this fortnight steady: ratio 1.04.

cases.name: slow gradual decline
cases.input: 8 weeks. Step-time ratio week by week: 1.04, 1.05, 1.07, 1.09, 1.12, 1.14, 1.17, 1.19. Cadence fell from 110 to 97 over the same weeks. Daytime walking only. No night events, pills all confirmed, no free-fall.

cases.name: bystander: are you OK
cases.input: Free-fall of 0.4 s then a 5 g impact at 2:14 pm; band horizontal afterwards. Band and app asked 'did you fall?'. No tap. Heard, voice not matching the wearer (0.12), close to the band: 'oh my god, are you OK? Don't move, let me help you up.' Wearer's voice (match 0.88): 'I think so... my hip hurts.'

cases.name: bystander: calls for help
cases.input: Free-fall of 0.4 s then a 5 g impact at 2:14 pm; band horizontal afterwards. Band and app asked 'did you fall?'. No tap. Heard, voice not matching the wearer (0.10), close to the band: 'Margaret! Margaret, can you hear me? Somebody call an ambulance!' Nothing from the wearer's voice. Band motion: none.

cases.name: bystander: she's fine, wearer silent
cases.input: Free-fall of 0.4 s then a 5 g impact at 2:14 pm; band horizontal afterwards. Band and app asked 'did you fall?'. No tap. Heard, voice not matching the wearer (0.15), close to the band: 'whoa, careful! You okay? Here, take my arm. She's fine, just slipped.' Nothing recognisable from the wearer's voice. Band motion: upright again after 40 seconds, slow walking.

cases.name: TV drama, no fall
cases.input: No free-fall and no impact; the band has been still on the wrist, wearer seated for 40 minutes. Heard, voice not matching the wearer (0.09), quiet and far from the band: 'oh my god, are you OK? Call an ambulance!' followed by music.

cases.name: dropped band, 'oops'
cases.input: Free-fall of 0.2 s then a 3 g impact at 9:02 am, two seconds after the band was taken off. Heard, wearer's voice (match 0.90), not distressed: 'oops, dropped it.' Band then picked up and put back on; normal walking.
